ROOT: EXACT TWO-FORM / MONOTONE CONSTITUTIVE INTERFACE FOR THE ORIGINAL QUARTIC
10 November2026 Brisbane. A sufficient full-gradient interface, not a quasiconvexity theorem or a claimed historically new general method.

Use the accepted original definitions k>1/3, ell=3k-1, n=k+1, m=3k+1, u=|F_col1|^2,v=|F_col2|^2,j=detF:
J_k(F)=ell(ku-v+2j)^2/(8n)+ell*u*v/4+j^2.
The completed monotone companion gives
lambda(F)=[3ell(ku-v)+24kj]/(2m),
L=(lambda-2j)/ell, T=DR-L cofF, R=(J-j^2)/ell.
Consequently DJ=ell*T+lambda*Dj, and
D^2J(F)[B,B]=ell DT(F)[B]:B+d_lambda(F)[B]*d_j(F)[B]+2lambda(F)detB.
Strict monotonicity ofT makes the first term nonnegative, but supplies no sign for the last two terms. This identifies the actual mixed work, rather than deleting a variable weighted minor.

The known constitutive curvature is d(T:dF)=-dL wedge dj. It is an EXACT two-form: -d(L dj). Thus it belongs to the same mathematical correction class as the heat-flow exact-form approach in Bruno-Pasqualotto2608.06367v1, without implying its correction already works for this anisotropic J.
For ANY homogeneous-quadratic two-form omega on R4=R^(2x2) satisfying d omega=0, let E be the radial vector field. Cartan's formula gives d(i_E omega)=4omega, hence omega=d alpha with cubic alpha=(i_E omega)/4. There are6 wedge pairs times10 quadratic monomials=60 initial coefficients. Closedness imposes linear coefficient equations (at most16); no positivity or sum-of-squares representation is thereby proved.

LetF=A+Dphi, phi:T2->R2 smooth periodic. Its actual compatible two-jets have
B1=[[a,b],[d,e]], B2=[[b,c],[e,f]].
The pullback ofomega is omega_F(B1,B2) dx1 wedge dx2, whose integral is0 by Stokes becauseomega is exact andF is periodic. This is an integrated derivative correction, NOT cancellation of the energy term lambda(F)detF/2.

Therefore the following actual pointwise certificate would suffice:
sum_(i=1,2) D^2J(F)[Bi,Bi]+omega_F(B1,B2)>=0
for EVERY F in R4 and EVERY(a,b,c,d,e,f).
It is a6x6 quadratic form in the two-jet variables with quadratic coefficients inF. Nonnegative biquadratic forms are not automatically sums of squares. An unsuccessful Gram/SDP search is not a negative theorem about this certificate class, much less about quasiconvexity.
